'''Leonidas''' (''Leon'') '''Alaoglu''' ({{langx|el|Λεωνίδας Αλάογλου}}; 1914–1981)<ref name=":5" /> was a Canadian-American [[mathematician]] and [[operations researcher]]. During his six-year stint as a mathematician from 1938 to 1944, Alaoglu studied several topics, including [[topology]], [[number theory]], and the geometry of [[Polyhedron|polyhedra]]. His best known result, which he proved during this period, was [[Alaoglu's theorem]] on the [[Weak topology|weak-star]] compactness of the closed [[Unit sphere|unit ball]] in the [[dual space|dual]] of a [[normed space]].<ref>American Men & Women of Science. 14th edition. New York: R.R. Bowker, 1979. There is no entry for him in the 15th or later editions</ref> After 1944, he left academia for the world of operations research.

== Life and work ==

=== Early life (1914–1938) ===
Alaoglu was born in 1914 in [[Red Deer, Alberta]], Canada, to [[Greek Canadians|Greek Canadian]] parents. He studied mathematics at the [[University of Alberta]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last=Mardešić |first=Sibe |author-link=Sibe Mardešić |date=2000 |title=Topology in Eastern Europe 1900–1950 |url=https://topology.nipissingu.ca/tp/reprints/v25/tp25127.pdf |journal=Topology Proceedings |volume=25}}</ref>

=== Education and mathematical career (1938–1944) ===
In 1938, Alaoglu received his PhD from the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our History {{!}} Department of Mathematics {{!}} The University of Chicago |url=https://mathematics.uchicago.edu/about/our-history/ |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=mathematics.uchicago.edu}}</ref> His dissertation was on ''Weak topologies of normed linear spaces'' and establishes [[Alaoglu's theorem]].<ref name=":1" /> He went on to spend one year at [[Pennsylvania State University]],<ref name=":6">
{{citation |last=Niven |first=Ivan |title=A Century of Mathematics in America |date=1989 |page=219 |editor-last=Duren |editor-first=Peter L. |display-editors=etal |chapter=The Threadbare Thirties |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8KnZjdBlw14C&q=leonidas+alaoglu+american&pg=PA219 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=0821801244}}</ref> then went on to [[Harvard University]] between 1939 and 1941 and to [[Purdue University]] between 1942 and 1944.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":1" />

=== Operations research career (1944–1981) ===
In 1944, in the midst of World War II, Alaoglu left academia to become an [[Operations research|operations analyst]] for the [[United States Air Force]].<ref name=":6" /> In 1946, he gained [[Citizenship of the United States|U.S. citizenship]].<ref name=":5" />

On August 21, 1947, Alaoglu married teacher Cleo Alaoglu (1915–2016).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Obituary for Cleo Alaoglu at Greek Obituary |url=https://www.greekobituary.net/obituary/3637853?lud=5109D2D205DCB726133EFB1F7A435F87 |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=www.greekobituary.net |language=en}}</ref> The couple would go on to have three children, raising them in the [[Encino, Los Angeles|Encino]] district of Los Angeles as well as in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref name=":0" />

In 1952, Anaoglu attended the founding meeting of the [[Operations Research Society of America]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1952 |title=Members Attending the Founding Meeting |url=https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/opre.1.1.26 |journal=Journal of the Operations Research Society of America |language=en |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=26–27 |doi=10.1287/opre.1.1.26 |issn=0096-3984}}</ref> In 1953, he joined the Operations Research Division of the [[Lockheed Corporation]] as a mathematician, where he worked ever since, until he eventually died in 1981.<ref name=":5" />

=== Legacy ===
Beginning in 1983, [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] instituted the annual "Leonidas Alaoglu Memorial Lecture in Mathematics" in Alaoglu's honor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leonidas Alaoglu Memorial Lecture in Mathematics {{!}} The Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy |url=https://www.pma.caltech.edu/research-and-academics/mathematics/mathematics-seminars/leonidas-alaoglu-memorial-lecture-in-mathematics |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=www.pma.caltech.edu}}</ref>

== Research ==

=== Topology and analysis ===
In 1938, Alaoglu proved in his PhD thesis that, in the [[dual space]] of a [[Banach space]] under the [[weak-star topology]], the [[closed unit ball]] is [[Compact (mathematics)|compact]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Mac Lane |first=Saunders |author-link=Saunders Mac Lane |date=2012 |title=Mathematics at the University of Chicago: A Brief History |url=https://celebratio.org/media/essaypdf/68_main_1.pdf |journal=Celebratio Mathematica}}</ref> His thesis was at the [[University of Chicago]] with [[Lawrence M. Graves]].<ref name=":1" />

In 1940, Alaoglu gave a general theory of [[Weak convergence (Hilbert space)|weak convergence]] in a [[normed linear space]] in his PhD thesis using the notion of a [[directed set]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Alaoglu |first=Leon |date=1940 |title=Weak Topologies of Normed Linear Spaces |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1968829 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=41 |issue=1 |pages=252–267 |doi=10.2307/1968829 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In particular, he constructed a [[universal Banach space]], and also described how to integrate and differentiate functions which take values in an [[adjoint space]].<ref name=":2" />

In 1940, Alaoglu and [[Garrett Birkhoff]] proved two [[Ergodic theory|ergodic theorems]] (i.e., statements that sums of the form <math>\sum_g \lambda_g xT_g </math> for some [[Group (mathematics)|group]] or [[semigroup]] ''G'' of linear operators <math>T_g </math> on a Banach space ''E'' converge). The first one covers the case when <math>|xT_g|\leq |x| </math> and ''E'' is [[uniformly convex]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Alaoglu |first=L. |last2=Birkhoff |first2=G. |author2-link=Garrett Birkhoff|date=1940 |title=General Ergodic Theorems |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1969004 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=41 |issue=2 |pages=293–309 |doi=10.2307/1969004 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The second covers the case when the group is an "[[ergodic group]]", in the sense that there is an infinite series of [[Measure (mathematics)|measures]] on the group that is asymptotically invariant under both left-multiplication and right-multiplication.<ref name=":3" /> (This class includes ''n''-parameter [[abelian group]]s and all [[Lie group]]s which correspond to a [[nilpotent Lie algebra]].)<ref name=":3" />

=== Number theory ===
In 1944, Alaoglu and [[Paul Erdős]] studied the prime factorizations of [[superabundant number]]s and [[highly composite number]]s. In particular, for a highly [[abundant number]] <math>n = \prod_i p^{k_p}</math>, they gave the estimate <math>\log(1 + 1/k_p) > \log q\log 2/\log p + O(\delta) </math>, where the error term behaves as <math>(\log\log p)^3/(\log p)^3 </math> for small ''q'' and <math>1/q^{1 - \theta}\log p </math> for larger ''q''.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Alaoglu |first1=L. |last2=Erdös |first2=P. |author2-link=Paul Erdős|date=1944 |title=On Highly Composite and Similar Numbers |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1990319 |journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=56 |issue=3 |pages=448–469 |doi=10.2307/1990319 |issn=0002-9947|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In doing so, they made use of [[Albert Ingham]] and [[Guido Hoheisel]]'s result that the density of the prime numbers is the same in intervals <math>(q, q + cq^{\theta}) </math> for some <math>\theta < 1 </math>.<ref name=":4" /> The same year, Alaoglu and Erdős discussed a 1932 conjecture of [[Paul Poulet]] that iterating the function <math>\phi(\sigma(n))</math> where <math>\phi </math> is the [[totient function]] and <math>\sigma </math> is the [[Divisor function|sum-of-divisors function]] eventually leads to a cycle. Using tables originally provided by [[James Whitbread Lee Glaisher]], they verified the conjecture up to <math>n < 10,000</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alaoglu |first=Leon |last2=Erdös |first2=Paul |date=1944 |title=A conjecture in elementary number theory |url=https://www.ams.org/bull/1944-50-12/S0002-9904-1944-08257-8/ |journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=50 |issue=12 |pages=881–882 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1944-08257-8 |issn=0002-9904|doi-access=free }}</ref>

=== Geometry ===
In 1946, Alaoglu and [[John H. Giese]] constructed [[Uniform polyhedron|uniform]], [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] polyhedra that were topologically equivalent to a [[torus]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alaoglu |first=Leonidas |last2=Giese |first2=J. H. |date=1946 |title=Uniform Isohedral Tori |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2306079 |journal=[[The American Mathematical Monthly]] |volume=53 |issue=1 |pages=14–17 |doi=10.2307/2306079 |issn=0002-9890}}</ref>
